parsed.explanation: The parent regime imposes a universal-exposure document regime: passports now record sex at birth, the foreign ministry tags suspected trans applicants for refusal and possible fraud-based ineligibility, and X-marker processing has stopped — an exposure every trans visitor crosses at entry, with documented confiscations and strandings. The parent also restricts facility access across a growing number of states/provinces and documents custody harms. This state/province adds a strong protective layer: a 2023 shield law covering gender-affirming care, anti-discrimination law since 1993, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, a trans panic defence ban, X markers on licences without documentation, and care coverage — placing it in the protective tier of the 2026 risk assessment. Under the parent, the visitor keeps the passport/entry exposure regardless of local protections; the dated 2012 custody case and unresolved shield-law application weigh modestly. The protective machinery raises the score above the parent's average, but the enforced national document regime caps it: ~0.55.
